newsitem.title: INDIA: Plane hijackers did not transit in Bombay - official.
newsitem.headline: Plane hijackers did not transit in Bombay - official.

text.p: The hijackers of an Ethiopian Airlines plane, which plunged into the sea off the Comoro Islands leaving at least 50 people dead, did not transit in Bombay, an Indian airport official said on Sunday.

Ethiopian Airline officials had said the hijackers were believed to be transit passengers from Bombay. They said the identity of the hijackers was not confirmed but that they may have wanted to hijack the plane to Australia.
But Arun Mehen, airport manager at the Sahar International Airport in Bombay, said: "No, no ... they (hijackers) were not from here (in transit in Bombay)."
An Ethiopian Airlines spokeswoman said 58 died when the plane crashed off the Comoro Islands after running out of fuel on Saturday and 52 people were known to have survived.
The Boeing 767 had 175 passengers and crew aboard when it went down near the Indian Ocean archipelago off the coast of Mozambique. The fate of the 65 others was not yet known.

The pilot of the plane, Leul Abate, said the airliner was hijacked by three men. "They may be either Ethiopian, Djiboutian or Somalian -- they spoke French," Leul said from his hospital bed at Moroni on the Comoro Islands.
But Mehen said there were no Ethiopians among the 42 passengers who transited from Bombay before boarding the aircraft in Addis Ababa.
Mehen said the passengers originating from Bombay included 19 Indians, nine Sri Lankans, nine Nigerians, three Americans, one from the Ivory Coast and another unidentified person.
